title: Inspired by Braid: a time-rewinding puzzle-platformer built with Claude Code agents
author: rip222
selftext:
Braid is one of my all-time favourites, and I always wanted to make something with that feel: time as the puzzle, a sad little story in bits of text. So I tried doing it with AI agents.



It's called Still Hour. It's set in a drowned city where all the clocks stopped. You can rewind the whole level whenever you want (yes, like Braid), and you also get two of my own tools. You can freeze one moving thing (a frozen moth = a platform), or leave an echo of yourself that replays your moves, so it can stand on a plate while you run through the door.



I did all the puzzles myself. Claude Code agents wrote basically all the code, with each one owning a piece (engine, levels, art, UI, audio, story). What kept it from falling apart was one big design doc they all had to follow, with exact numbers like "max ledge is 3 tiles, max gap is 5", so the levels actually fit the puzzles.



The thing I learned: agents can't really playtest by watching. So the game logic is deterministic and runs without a browser, every level comes with scripts that beat it and grab all the secrets, and a test tool yells if anything breaks. That saved me a ton of time.



No AI images btw. The art is all built in code, and the music plays backwards when you rewind, which I'm way too happy about.



It's free in the browser: [https://app.deadsimple.games/games/stillhour](https://app.deadsimple.games/games/stillhour)



20 levels. Ask me anything about the puzzles or the workflow.

comments.author: CrowdGoesWildWoooo
comments.body:
Proof read your game, some text alignment aren’t pretty.

Fix the way the main character walk, currently it looks like naruto run. You can easily prompt a sprite sheet with better running animation

replies.author: rip222
replies.body:
hahaha I didn't think of it this way, I was too focused on puzzles and level design. But fair enough I will address naruto run and the text alignment.   
It's not a sprite though, it's a 3d object.  
Also if you can explain what exactly bothers you about text it would be pretty cool, as I'm not a ux or typography expert.

Thanks for feedback <3

replies.author: CrowdGoesWildWoooo
replies.body:
Ah it’s minor, just for reminder.

The “Touch once to leave a mark …” has right alignment while the rest of the game are center aligned text.

This looks good btw. Even if you tell me this is not made with AI I’d believe you, it’s quite well polished.

replies.author: rip222
replies.body: nah I want to be honest about it, but I wasted way too many tokens to make it look like it does xD
